claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys at temperatures below approximately 1000 K.
Diffuse antiphase boundaries act as potent phonon-scattering centers.
The SRO-induced suppression of lattice thermal conductivity diminishes above approximately 1500 K.
At high temperature, thermal entropy disrupts SRO and restores phonon mean free paths toward those of a random solid solution.
MoNbTaW can be compared in SRO and random-solid-solution states at the same composition.
Annealing MoNbTaW at approximately 800 K, followed by quenching or slow cooling, induces and stabilizes SRO.
SRO in MoNbTaW creates diffuse antiphase boundaries.
DAPBs are interfaces between chemically ordered regions.
DAPBs disrupt the periodicity of the lattice potential.
Breaking local chemical order during screw-dislocation glide creates DAPBs with an energy cost.
The energy cost associated with local order produces a fluctuating potential landscape that scatters phonons and reduces lattice thermal conductivity.
Increasing temperature reduces the relative influence of the SRO enthalpic contribution through the entropy term in the free-energy barrier.
Increasing temperature decreases DAPB density or the phonon-scattering cross-section of DAPBs.
Between 300 and 1000 K, the lattice thermal conductivity of the SRO state is lower than that of the random-solid-solution state.
The thermal-conductivity difference between SRO and RSS states decreases toward zero as temperature approaches 2000 K.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to temperatures below the order-disorder transition, where SRO remains stable.
Long-range precipitation would introduce grain-boundary or phase-boundary scattering distinct from DAPB scattering.
The cited evidence addresses dislocation mobility and SRO strengthening rather than phonon or thermal transport.
The application of DAPB physics to phonon scattering is an extrapolation whose magnitude and characteristic disruption temperature are not quantified by the cited records.
A same-composition comparison of SRO and RSS samples, with SRO independently measured, can test the predicted conductivity ordering and high-temperature convergence.

contradictions.description: The intervention and structural-mediator fields portray DAPBs as pre-existing interfaces created directly by annealing-induced ordered regions, whereas the mechanism—and the cited evidence—portrays DAPBs as defects generated when local order is broken during dislocation glide.
